questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`for number in range(3):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`print(number)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`count = 0` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`while count < 2:` — Repeats while a condition holds; without the loop work happens once, and an unchanged condition can loop forever.
`count += 1` — Updates an existing result; without it, a counter or total stays unchanged.
